answer: Each identity binds one genome in the ivory registry: a lab signs a 200-SNP panel hash, with a 30 POA bond locked 90 days. A genome shared by two identities loses both bonds. Each epoch a random 12-SNP bridge check needs lab proof within 72 hours, matching above 0.98; two misses forfeit half the bond and freeze payouts 3 epochs. 100 fakes need 100 genomes at $99 each plus 3,000 POA locked; brokered genomes follow a spiral price curve doubling every 50 sold, so the 100th costs 4 times the first. Twins share one genome and pass a joint in-person check. Verifiers replay all hashes on-chain.
